Gen.G and Bilibili Gaming meet in the League of Legends Worlds 2026 final at 2 p.m. ET Saturday at Barclays Center in Brooklyn, the first Worlds final without T1 since 2021. (Photo by Bruce Bennett/Getty Images) Gen.G and Bilibili Gaming meet in the League of Legends Worlds 2026 final at 2 p.m. ET Saturday at Barclays Center in Brooklyn, the first Worlds final without T1 since 2021. The start time and venue were previously reported on the official LoL Esports schedule . Spilled.gg noted that this is the first final without T1 since 2021, and that every Worlds final from 2023 to 2025 featured T1 and peaked above 6 million viewers. BLG-T1 Semifinal Set the Tournament Peak Prensa Esports , citing Esports Charts, said the tournament peak so far is 3,605,295 concurrent viewers for Bilibili Gaming's 3-1 semifinal win over T1 on Nov. 8. The firm does not include certain Chinese platforms in that figure, the outlet said. The same source listed a 2,193,252 peak for Gen.G's semifinal sweep of Invictus Gaming. Prensa Esports said those figures are estimates and can be revised. This website uses cookies to ensure you get the best experience on our website. Read our Privacy Policy . Okay Worlds 2026 Viewership By The Numbers 3,605,295 Peak Viewers For BLG-T1 Esports Charts had the Nov. 8 semifinal as the tournament peak so far, Prensa Esports said. Statistics 2,193,252 Peak For Gen.G-IG Gen.G's semifinal sweep of Invictus Gaming drew that peak, according to the same source. Statistics 6 Million-Plus For Each 2023-25 Final Every Worlds final from 2023 to 2025 featured T1 and peaked above that mark, Spilled.gg noted. Statistics First Final Without T1 Since 2021 T1's exit ended its bid for a fourth straight Worlds title. Statistics A Final Without the Recent Ratings Driver T1's exit ended a bid for a fourth straight title and removed the team that had anchored the last three finals' audiences. Saturday's series is still a best-of-five between an unbeaten Gen.G side and a Bilibili Gaming team that has already beaten T1, Dplus KIA and Hanwha Life Esports at this Worlds. Sergey Demidov is a veteran sports journalist with over 18 years of experience covering international sports. Since beginning his career in 2007, he has reported on the Olympic Games (Sochi 2014), FIFA World Cup (2014), UEFA Euro (2012), World Cup of Hockey (2016), and Stanley Cup Finals (since 2017).

Before joining RG, Sergey was an independent senior editor at NHL.com/ru (2016–present) and contributed to Gazeta.ru and TASS News Agency. Currently, he leads RG’s global news desk, overseeing correspondents across North America, Europe, Africa, Asia, and South America.

He has conducted one-on-one interviews with elite athletes, including Jaromir Jagr and Alex Ovechkin, former WADA and FIFA presidents Craig Reedie and Sepp Blatter, and soccer coaches like Fabio Capello.

Sergey’s editorial work emphasizes accuracy, sourcing transparency, and a neutral voice, aligned with the Trust Project and Google Publisher Center principles.

He is bilingual in English and Russian, specializing in NHL hockey.
